title: RSC Server-to-Client Boundary Serialization Validator
concept: Boundary Serialization Rules & Non-Serializable Props Rejection
problemStatement: Implement `validateRscBoundaryProps(props)` that recursively inspects props passed to a Client Component from a Server Component. It must return `{ valid: true }` for JSON-serializable primitives/arrays/objects and throw a descriptive TypeError if a function or non-serializable symbol is detected.
interviewTrap: You cannot pass an onClick handler function from a Server Component to a Client Component because Server Components cannot send executable JavaScript across the network wire.

testCases.name: Throws TypeError when passing functions across boundary
testCases.expected: Cannot pass function across Server-to-Client boundary at prop: onClick
testCases.testFn: try { validateRscBoundaryProps({ onClick: () => {} }); return 'no-error'; } catch (e) { return e.message; }

testCases.name: Detects deeply nested non-serializable properties with exact path

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What types can and CANNOT be passed as props across the Server-to-Client component boundary in RSC?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Props passed from Server Components to Client Components ('use client') MUST be serializable by the Flight protocol: strings, numbers, booleans, null, undefined, plain objects, arrays, Dates, Maps, Sets, TypedArrays, and Server Actions (`'use server'`). You CANNOT pass functions (like `onClick`), class instances, or Symbols across the boundary; doing so throws a serialization error.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Crucial boundary enforcement question for Next.js App Router.

realWorldUseCases.description: Passing an asynchronous server action (`'use server'`) as an action prop to a client form component.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: // Server Component passes server action to Client Button: <ClientButton onAction={serverAction} />

howToExplain.opening: The Server-to-Client boundary requires strict serialization of props because data traverses an HTTP network boundary between server and client.
keyPoints: Primitives, plain objects, arrays, and Dates are serializable.
Functions and class instances cannot cross the boundary.
Server Actions ('use server') are serializable as endpoint IDs.
Enforces clean separation between server computation and client UI.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Understanding serialization boundaries prevents runtime Flight crashes when mixing server and client components.
analogies: Shipping goods through international customs: raw ingredients (serializable data) pass through inspection; living animals or hazardous machinery (functions/closures) are stopped at the border.

commonMistakes.mistake: Passing an event handler onClick={() => {}} from a Server Component to a Client Component.
commonMistakes.why: Functions cannot be serialized over the wire; throws 'Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components'.
commonMistakes.correct: Declare the event handler inside the Client Component.

followUpDeepDive.question: How do Server Actions bypass the function serialization restriction?
followUpDeepDive.answer: A Server Action is not serialized as code; it is transformed by the compiler into an opaque action ID string (`$$typeof: Symbol.for('react.server.reference')`). When invoked on the client, React sends an HTTP POST request with that action ID back to the server.
followUpDeepDive.specReference: React RFC: Server Actions & Server References
